verdicts.summary: The combined rev-parse result is used only when the exit code is 0 or 1 and stdout has exactly 2 path lines plus the HEAD line (when HEAD exists) and a trailing empty line. Every other output goes to the old separate commands. HEAD detection gives the same result as the old hasHeadCommit, and the lost retry wrapper never applied to the old commands this call replaces.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases. (1) Git older than 2.31 echoes '--path-format=absolute' as an extra line: 5 lines with HEAD, 4 when unborn (exit 1). Neither matches the expected 4 or 3, so the code falls back and headExists still comes from the exit code. (2) A cwd containing a newline adds a line to both the common-dir and index paths, so the count is at least +2 and it falls back. A newline cannot be offset by a missing line, because the line count expected is set by the exit code. (3) An empty or corrupt HEAD ref after a crash: '--verify --quiet' exits 1, so headExists is false, the same as the old '--verify HEAD' failing with 128. (4) A transient failure or exit 128 skips VcsProcess's capture retry (VcsProcess.ts:361) because allowNonZeroExit is set. The old resolveGitCommonDir used a different operation label and was never retried either. The fallback inline index rev-parse at :943 is still retried as before. The index path is read without commitEnv in both versions, so GIT_INDEX_FILE does not differ.
